caption: A thin sheet-metal door is knocked on, and the panel visibly flexes and rattles under the knocks before going quiet.

sa.check: The door is knocked on: a hand raps the panel.
The panel flexes and rattles with the knocks.
The panel goes still after the knocking.
The knocking is a series of raps rather than a single blow.
The flexing comes with the knocks and the stillness follows the last knock.

pc.expect: The panel is still before the first knock; each flex begins as the knuckles land; the panel does not move by itself between or after knocks.
pc.fail: The panel is already shaking before the hand reaches it; or flexes while the hand is drawn back and away; or the hand raps and the panel stays rigid; or the door starts rattling again after it has gone still with nothing touching it.

pc.expect: Each knock's shake fades before or as the next knock lands, and after the last knock the rattle dies away to stillness.
pc.fail: The rattle grows after the knocking stops; or keeps the same shaking for the whole clip after the last knock; or the panel stops dead from a hard shake the instant the hand leaves it.

pc.expect: The panel flexes as a thin sheet: it dimples inward at the knuckles and springs back flat; the frame and hinges stay rigid.
pc.fail: A dimple stays pressed in after the hand lifts; or the panel folds like cloth; or the door frame bends with each knock; or a wave rolls across the whole panel like water.

pc.expect: The wall, the door frame and any neighbouring panels stay still; only the knocked panel shivers.
pc.fail: The wall beside the door shakes; or a neighbouring panel rattles while the knocked one is still; or the door frame jumps in the wall.

pc.expect: One door with its panel, frame and handle; the hand passes through nothing and the door stays one piece.
pc.fail: The hand passes into or through the panel; or the panel splits or a hole opens where the hand lands; or the handle vanishes or moves to another spot; or the door changes into another object.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The door's paint, any rust or marks on it, and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The door changes colour; or marks and scratches on it shift or vanish; or the surroundings change.
